solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vim in clothing an unusual dog

parts.note: a getup is an outfit, a set of clothes

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters of dog are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A dog dressed up in a strange outfit, full of vim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' is the anagram signal for 'dog'; 'clothing' is a noun here, an outfit, not a container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Vim is energy and drive, which is what get-up-and-go means as an idiom.

clue.text: Novelist with wobbly gut? Never!

indicators.note: a wobbly thing is unsteady and shaken about, so the letters of gut and never are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer protesting that they will never have a flabby belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbly' rearranges GUT plus NEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was a Russian writer of novels such as Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Dutch feel sad in our absence?

definitions.meaning: 'Dutch' is old Cockney slang for a wife, short for 'duchess'
to feel sad in our absence is to ..., read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone from the Netherlands pining for us while we are away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like the nationality but is old London slang for one's wife; the second half is split MISS US.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is informal for wife, the same person called one's 'old Dutch' in Cockney speech.

clue.text: Soft stuff in a kind of white meat

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for softly

indicators.note: the word in places the cramming inside the wine's name

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont
to stuff is to ram or cram

explanation.surface: Something soft packed inside white meat, like a stuffed chicken breast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white meat' reads as one phrase, but 'white' is the wine ASTI and only 'meat' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a cured, smoked beef, served sliced as a deli meat.

clue.text: Hostile states close to Delaware

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly, so avers means states

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its last letter is taken

explanation.surface: Unfriendly US states lying near Delaware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'states' looks like a noun about America but is the verb AVERS; 'close to' takes the last letter of Delaware.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed or hostile to it.

clue.text: Family member you heard laugh makes a racket

parts.note: bro is short for brother

indicators.note: heard tells us the word is taken by its sound, giving a single letter that is pronounced the same

parts.note: the word you is said aloud
ha-ha is a laugh

explanation.surface: A sibling's guffaw causes a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns YOU into the letter U, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion or fuss, the same sense as a racket meaning din.

clue.text: Stand-in governor, say, cutting regular payment

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside, so the abbreviation goes within the payment

parts.note: rent is paid regularly to a landlord
e.g. means 'for example', which 'say' also means

explanation.surface: A deputy official slashing someone's regular income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' is the insertion signal; 'say' supplies the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent governs on behalf of a monarch who is absent or too young, a ruling deputy.

clue.text: Country rejecting English in fact

indicators.note: rejecting means turning away, so one letter is dropped from the word for country

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A nation refusing English, as a matter of fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' drops E from STATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stat is a statistic, a numerical fact.

clue.text: Maastricht Treaty idea — it won't fly!

definitions.meaning: the Maastricht Treaty set out European Monetary Union

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismissing a European treaty plan as doomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it won't fly' sounds like a dismissal of the plan but literally describes the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: EMU abbreviates European Monetary Union, the single-currency project agreed at Maastricht; the emu bird is flightless.

clue.text: Trendy figure breaking plug, which is accidental

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: breaking into a word means splitting it, so the number goes inside the publicity

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advert
ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A fashionable number interrupting an advert by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' signals insertion; 'figure' is a number, not a shape or a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inadvertent is unintentional, done by accident.

clue.text: Drives empty Subaru around, in which reg is wrong

indicators.note: in which says the next part sits inside the pair
turning around means facing the other way, so the remaining pair is read backwards
emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only its outer letters
being wrong means not in its proper order, so the letters of reg are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drives an empty Subaru with the wrong registration plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps the car's outer letters, 'around' turns that pair backwards, and 'is wrong' shuffles 'reg' to sit 'in which' the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Urges as a verb means drives on or impels, a synonym of drives.

clue.text: Unsteady from posh sort of wine knocked back fast

indicators.note: knocked back reads as 'drunk', but here sends the pair back to front

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in 'U and non-U'
brut describes very dry champagne or sparkling wine
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Wobbly after downing smart dry wine too quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but reverses UBRUT to TURBU; 'fast' is the noun, the period of Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent means disturbed and agitated, like unsteady air on a flight.

clue.text: Failure to recall men deployed in the east

indicators.note: in places the shuffled men within the continent

parts.note: Asia is the continent of the East

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out and rearranged, so the letters of men are shuffled

explanation.surface: Soldiers sent out East who cannot remember anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' is the anagram signal for 'men'; 'the east' gives a whole continent, which wraps round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, an inability to remember.

clue.text: Keep going through melted ice — it's fluid

indicators.note: going through means passing inside, so the verb sits within the rearranged ice
melted ice loses its shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to last is to keep going, to endure

explanation.surface: Something that lasts through melting ice, being liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'melted' shuffles 'ice' and 'through' puts the verb for keep going inside it; 'fluid' means flexible, not liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluid in the sense of flexible and adaptable matches elastic, as in an elastic schedule.

clue.text: Right-winger and Democrat with key objective to be superior

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a right-wing UK party
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A conservative and a democrat sharing one key aim of looking down on others.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is short for Conservative, the UK's main right-wing party.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend is to behave in a patronising way, acting as though superior to others.

clue.text: Branching out in papers about writing poetry

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: ID means identity papers
versification is the writing of verse

explanation.surface: Expanding into a new field by publishing poems in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ID into DI.
explanation.definitionFit: Diversification is spreading into new areas of activity, as a branch grows away from the trunk.

clue.text: Ready to catch curiously deep wind instrument

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside, so ripe surrounds the shuffled letters

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

indicators.note: curiously means oddly, so the letters of deep are arranged strangely

explanation.surface: Prepared to capture an oddly deep-sounding instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' shuffles 'deep'; 'to catch' has the word for ready hold those letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed pipe is a simple woodwind made from a reed, or an organ pipe with a vibrating reed.

clue.text: Setter's large drinking receptacle for drinking

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so setter's is I'M (I am)

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the container goes inside the word for large

parts.note: big means large
a bin is a container

explanation.surface: A setter says they own a large container to drink from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' appears twice: the first signals insertion (one word taking in another), the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Imbibing is a formal or jocular word for consuming alcohol.

clue.text: Sacrifice one million, constructing a motel

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: constructing means building, so the letters of a motel are put together anew

explanation.surface: Giving up a million to build a motel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructing' makes MOLATE from A MOTEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To immolate is to kill as an offering, especially by fire, a form of sacrifice.

clue.text: Story's rewritten about European aphrodisiac?

definitions.note: singular in the clue, while the answer is plural; the question mark covers the looseness

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reordered letters go round the abbreviation
a rewritten story has its parts put in new places, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A romantic tale revised around a European love potion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' turns STORYS into OYSTRS, placed 'about' E.
explanation.definitionFit: Oysters have a long reputation for arousing desire, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Primarily scruffy stroke in such handwriting?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A messy pen stroke in an untidy hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' looks like a pen mark but is the swimming CRAWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is messy, hurried writing.

clue.text: Greeting old lady, unfortunately the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means facing backwards, so the words are read in reverse

parts.note: one's old lady is one's mother, ma
alas is an exclamation of misfortune

explanation.surface: Saying hello to an elderly woman awkwardly, regrettably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns MAALAS into SALAAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Salaam is a respectful greeting in Muslim countries, meaning 'peace'.

clue.text: British stranger hasn't right kind of accent

indicators.note: hasn't means lacks, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: rummy means odd, so rummier means stranger

explanation.surface: A British oddball whose accent is not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun but is the comparative RUMMIER; 'hasn't' removes one R. Brummie is the accent of Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Brummie describes the speech of Birmingham people, a recognisable regional accent.

clue.text: A French king's housing I'm amazed to open

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the exclamation sits within the other letters

parts.note: un is French for a
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess
cor is a British exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A French king expressing amazement as he opens something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' has the French article plus the king's letter hold the exclamation; cor is British slang for surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncork is to open a bottle by drawing its cork.

clue.text: Staff put on kit? They take it off here

indicators.note: put on means placed after in an across entry, so the stick follows the kit

parts.note: a strip is a sports team's kit
a club is a heavy stick or staff

explanation.surface: Employees getting dressed, while elsewhere others undress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as employees but is a stick, CLUB; STRIP is a British word for a team's sports kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip club is a venue where performers remove their clothes, taking it all off.

clue.text: Determined husband makes third child

parts.note: set means fixed or determined

explanation.surface: A resolute husband fathers a third child.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Seth is the third son born to Adam and Eve, after Cain and Abel.

clue.text: Windy complaint from officer in charge

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, an officer

explanation.surface: A commanding officer grumbling about wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is abdominal pain often caused by trapped gas, an ailment of the windy sort.

clue.text: Maybe Le Corbusier's name in new plant or works

definitions.note: Maybe Le Corbusier's reads as 'Le Corbusier is, for example, a', with the 's standing for is

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation within the rearranged letters
works here means 'operates on', so the letters of new plant or are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: An architect's name appearing on a new factory or industrial works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges NEW PLANT OR into TOWPLANNER, with N put 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Corbusier, the Swiss-French architect, designed whole cities such as Chandigarh: an example of an urban designer.

clue.text: Fish with 25% cut in VAT

indicators.note: cut means removed, so that quarter is taken off the fish

parts.note: tuna is a fish
a quarter of a four-letter fish is one letter, its last

explanation.surface: Fish with a quarter of the sales tax taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'VAT' looks like the UK sales tax, Value Added Tax, but is a large cask.
explanation.definitionFit: A tun is a large cask for beer or wine, and a vat is a large tank or barrel.
